The Problem

Every year, millions cross borders and lose something they spent a lifetime building — their financial reputation.

Credit history, proof of income, and insurance records remain locked inside national systems — even when the underlying behavior hasn't changed. A person can be financially responsible their entire life, move abroad, and overnight become "credit invisible."

The problem works in both directions. Destination countries can't access foreign financial data. Origin countries can't verify what their emigrated customers report — they receive self-submitted PDFs with no way to authenticate them. Years of perfect financial history, locked on both sides.

👤

INDIVIDUALS

Migrants are treated as unknown or high-risk despite years of responsible financial behavior. They face higher deposits, worse rates, denied credit and insurance — for apartments, loans, and basic financial services in their new country.

🏦

DESTINATION BANKS

Have no access to foreign financial data — credit scores, income records, insurance history are trapped in origin-country systems. They reject good customers or take blind risk. Result: lost revenue from creditworthy applicants.

🏢

ORIGIN BANKS

Emigrating customers want mortgages, investments, and insurance back home — but banks cannot verify their current financial status abroad. They receive unverifiable PDFs. Lifetime value walks out with every departing customer.

This is not a problem of creditworthiness — it is a problem of data access and verifiability.

Market Size

304 million migrants globally. More than 70% can't carry their financial identity across borders.

Migration has almost doubled since 2000. Add ~40M digital nomads whose finances span borders without formally immigrating.

Our Solution

So we built it — one platform that aggregates, verifies, translates, and transfers financial identity between countries.

We combine credit portability (translating foreign credit scores), bank data aggregation (connecting bank accounts cross-border via open banking), and a consumer marketplace — all working in both directions. No competitor combines all three.

1

CONSUMER PERMISSION

Customer authorizes data sharing via our bank-branded app or magic link — fully consent-driven, GDPR compliant

2

DATA AGGREGATION

We pull credit bureau data + open banking transaction history from origin and/or destination country

3

TRANSLATION LAYER

Data normalized to destination country format — credit scores mapped, income verified, insurance history translated

4

BANK DASHBOARD

Bank sees complete verified financial profile in a customizable SaaS portal with AI-powered risk analysis

➡️ INBOUND BRIDGE

Destination banks underwrite newcomers. Example: UAE bank approves car loan for Indian professional using verified Indian credit + banking history.

⬅️ OUTBOUND BRIDGE

Origin banks retain emigrating customers. Example: Georgian bank provides mortgage to customer living in Germany, verified via German bank data.

Why Now

The timing couldn't be better: open banking is scaling, post-COVID mobility is surging, and the EU Regulation CCD2 accelerates the need.

01

05
Regional Bank Expansion — TBC → Uzbekistan (Payme, 18M users). BOG → Armenia (Ameriabank, $304M). Kaspi.kz → Turkey ($1.13B). Every expansion = more demand.

The Bottom Line

Cross-border financial identity will be built. The question is who builds it for the 230 million still waiting.

Nova Credit is US-focused and pivoting toward domestic cashflow data. Mifundo covers only intra-EU. Goscore serves Scandinavian corridors. CreditChek focuses on Africa to US/UK. Each solves a piece — none connects the full picture. 5vly is the only platform architected from day one to be bidirectional, multi-corridor, and built for both B2B and B2C — with signed contracts from two banks covering ~80% of our launch market, and a founder who lived the problem and spent 17 years inside the banks we sell to.
